name: Prepare and run candidate searches
summary: Gather terms, optionally generate five, then run bounded searches and return separate attributable attempts.

steps.label: Choose the search approach
steps.human:
Choose one or more compatible offered keyword/vector search contracts for the original question, within the main plan and remaining budget. Select useful known component filters. This is not an instruction to run all methods or to execute them concurrently. Unsupported vector readiness excludes that method.

I/O boundary: Known needs and trusted kernel scope are reusable inputs. Needs source_scope is semantic metadata and never broadens Scope authority.

steps.label: Gather supplied or known terms
steps.human:

Prepare each selected contract separately. Reuse terms only where that contract accepts their meaning and scope; preserve their binding to query/version/source.

steps.label: Run separate retrieval attempts
steps.human:
Execute the permitted bounded searches once. Keep each attempt separate: original question, method/query/version, terms, component filters, source/revision, model/version where relevant, budget, evidence locators, coverage and outcome. Do not combine candidates yet. Empty evidence, denied access, outage, missing mapping and partial coverage remain distinct. Structurally valid but semantically rejected terms do not execute. Preserve the main attempt history and cumulative budget; selecting multiple searches does not imply parallel execution. Return useful evidence even if another attempt fails. Use only the inputs validated and accepted for that specific method/query contract.

I/O boundary: Known per-operation output fields are shown as a reference. This recipe result example is not a keyword/vector receipt or evidence that the new five-term fanout executes.

Traversal and multiple-method design extension
Added bounded method selection/return routes and a shared attempt-comparison handoff. Target specification only; no runtime or acceptance-status change.

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.
